summary: AeroShield is an interactive decision-support web application that bridges over two decades of disparate MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) satellite active fire records into a unified 24-year fire activity calendar. To eliminate the artificial post-2012 detection spikes caused by combining different sensor resolutions, AeroShield uses a 1 km² spatial grid normalization algorithm that aligns historical and modern observations. Beyond accurate seasonal anomaly tracking, the system integrates live NASA FIRMS hotspots, NASA POWER wind vectors, and NASA SRTM terrain slope data to project 90-minute fire spread corridors, calculate safe upwind evacuation routes, and dispatch automated GeoJSON and offline GPS SMS alerts to civilians. This matters because it transforms fragmented Earth observation archives into life-saving intelligence—protecting vulnerable forest communities, wildlife, and emergency responders before and during wildfire crises.
details:
THE CHALLENGE & PROBLEM:

For over two decades, NASA satellites have monitored global active fire hotspots. However, historical records are fragmented across two distinct sensor generations: MODIS (1 km resolution, active since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m resolution, active since 2012). Because VIIRS detects smaller, lower-intensity fires at a much higher spatial density, raw historical comparisons create artificial detection spikes after 2012—preventing land managers and emergency responders from seeing an accurate, consistent picture of wildfire seasonality and anomalies.

WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS (TRI-MODULE ARCHITECTURE):

Developed by Team AeroShield at Çubuk BİLSEM (Science and Art Center) in Ankara, Turkey, AeroShield is an interactive decision-support web application that transforms fragmented satellite observations into life-saving intelligence:

  1. Harmonized Fire Activity Calendar: Using a spatial grid normalization algorithm ($0.01^\circ \times 0.01^\circ$ / $\approx 1\text{ km}^2$ reference cell clustering), AeroShield aligns high-resolution daily VIIRS detections with historical MODIS records. Users can explore a 24-year interactive heatmap calendar (2003–2026) and toggle between raw uncalibrated data and the normalized AeroShield Index to identify true seasonal fire peaks and anomalous weeks without sensor-induced bias.
  2. Dynamic Evacuation & Early Warning Engine: When live NASA FIRMS hotspots are detected during critical calendar periods, AeroShield integrates real-time wind vectors (NASA POWER) and terrain slope data (NASA SRTM) to project 90-minute fire and smoke spread corridors. It dynamically flags threatened downwind roads as closed and calculates safe upwind evacuation routes to open assembly hubs.
  3. Civic Alert & Cell-Broadcast Integration: Once an upwind evacuation corridor is computed, the built-in Civic Alert Dispatcher formats standardized GeoJSON polygons and concise, offline-ready GPS evacuation messages for national emergency Cell-Broadcast systems (such as AFAD) and regional SMS networks.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT:

AeroShield bridges the gap between complex Earth observation archives and immediate public safety. By eliminating the 2012 sensor artifact (removing ~73.9% of artificial post-2012 hotspot inflation in sample Mediterranean/Anatolian basins), authorities gain reliable multi-decade climate and fire trend intelligence. During active emergencies, vulnerable rural communities, forest villages, wildlife rescue teams, and first responders receive clear, actionable, upwind evacuation routes within minutes—reducing panic, preventing entrapment on smoke-logged roads, and saving lives.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED:

  • Frontend & Interactive Mapping: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, and Leaflet.js for interactive geospatial visualization.
  • Data Processing & Scientific Visualization: Python (Matplotlib, NumPy) for spatial grid harmonization modeling, statistical validation, and multi-decade trend charting.
  • NASA Open Data Sources: NASA FIRMS (MODIS Collection 6.1 & VIIRS 375m), NASA POWER API (wind speed, wind direction, temperature, relative humidity), and NASA SRTM (30m Digital Elevation Model).
  • Documentation & Media Prototyping: Standard desktop workstations, NotebookLM, and digital presentation tools for technical documentation and demonstration workflows.

CREATIVITY & KEY FACTORS CONSIDERED BY OUR TEAM:

  • End-to-End Integration: Rather than stopping at historical data visualization, AeroShield creatively connects 24-year retrospective climate analysis directly to real-time evacuation routing and citizen-level mobile alerts.
  • Physical & Topographic Realism: Our team accounted for the fact that wildfires accelerate upslope and travel rapidly along wind vectors, ensuring evacuation routes are strictly routed upwind and away from steep canyon bottlenecks.
  • Low-Connectivity Resilience: Recognizing that rural forest areas often lose high-speed internet during wildfires, we designed our civic alert messages around lightweight text instructions and offline-ready GPS coordinates.
